# Define the tutorial packaging format

## Description

Defines the packaging format that makes curated tutorials versioned and
testable independently of Dashboard releases: the metadata a tutorial package
carries, how images are pinned, and the validation manifest used to check that
a packaged tutorial is complete, conformant, and testable against a platform
release. This is a specification-defining epic: it produces the format and its
validation criteria, not the curated tutorials themselves — the notebook and
pipeline tutorials are authored separately, as packaged instances of this
format.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial packaging format, covering:
  - Package metadata: identity, journey description, and the launch
    characteristics the Dashboard needs to list a tutorial in the gallery and
    launch it into a user's project
  - Pinned images: how a tutorial package references specific image versions so
    it runs predictably across releases
  - Validation manifest: what is checked about a packaged tutorial and the
    pass/fail criteria, so conformance and testability are determinable
    without a Dashboard release
- Define versioning rules for tutorial packages, so a tutorial can be added,
  updated, or re-versioned without a Dashboard release
- Define how a packaged tutorial is validated against the manifest (what is
  checked, and what a passing result means), covering both tutorial kinds the
  gallery launches: notebook tutorials (opened in a workbench) and pipeline
  tutorials (imported into a project)
- Validate the format with a minimal stub fixture — synthetic metadata and
  placeholder content that exercises the schema end to end — before real
  tutorials are authored against it. The real curated tutorials are authored
  in the tutorial-authoring work, not here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written specification of the tutorial packaging format exists, covering
  package metadata, image pinning, and the validation manifest.
- A minimal stub fixture (synthetic metadata, placeholder content) passes the
  format's validation, demonstrating that package conformance can be checked
  mechanically.
- A package that violates the manifest fails validation with actionable
  diagnostics.
- A tutorial package version can change without any Dashboard release: the
  package carries its own version and image pins.
- The format supports both launch paths: notebook tutorials opened in a
  workbench, and pipeline tutorials imported into a project.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation
  manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently
  of Dashboard releases.
- Enables HLR-1 (P0) and HLR-2 (P0): the Dashboard gallery and the curated
  tutorials are both built against this format, so this epic inherits P0
  priority by priority inheritance (it is a prerequisite of all P0 work in
  this strategy).

# Author the curated notebook tutorials

## Description

Authors five curated, tested notebook tutorials covering the core
getting-started journeys — first workbench, data prep, first training run,
first deployment, and first RAG app — each packaged per the tutorial packaging
format so it can be listed in the Dashboard tutorial gallery and launched into
a user's project by opening a workbench with the notebook. This is substantive
content authoring: new, maintained tutorial notebooks, distinct from the
product code that implements the gallery and from the packaging format they
conform to.

## Scope

- Author five notebook tutorials, one per journey:
  1. First workbench — create a project and workbench, open the tutorial
     notebook
  2. Data prep — load and prepare data in a workbench
  3. First training run — train a model on the prepared data
  4. First deployment — serve the trained model
  5. First RAG app — build a first retrieval-augmented generation application
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest)
- Test each tutorial against the current platform release: each passes the
  format's validation and runs successfully end to end
- Keep tutorial content within platform capabilities available in the current
  release (tutorials must run against it as shipped)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist, one per journey listed above, each packaged
  per the tutorial packaging format.
- Each tutorial passes the packaging format's validation.
- Each tutorial is tested against the current release and runs successfully
  end to end in a user project.
- Each tutorial package carries the metadata and pinned images needed for the
  Dashboard to list it in the gallery and launch it into a project (opening a
  workbench with the notebook).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys, each
  tested against the current release — this epic covers the five
  notebook-based journeys; the first-pipeline journey is authored in the
  pipeline tutorial authoring work.

# Build the Dashboard tutorial gallery and one-click launch

## Description

Implements the product code in the Dashboard: a tutorial gallery section
listing curated tutorials, and one-click launch mechanics that launch a
selected tutorial into the user's own project — opening a workbench with the
tutorial notebook, or importing the tutorial pipeline. The gallery reads
tutorial packages conforming to the tutorial packaging format, so curated
tutorials can be added, updated, and versioned without Dashboard releases.

## Scope

- Add a tutorial gallery section to the Dashboard that lists tutorial packages
  conforming to the tutorial packaging format, rendering their metadata
- Implement one-click launch of a selected tutorial into the user's project:
  - Notebook tutorials: open a workbench in the user's project with the
    tutorial notebook
  - Pipeline tutorials: import the tutorial pipeline into the user's project
- Consume the tutorial packaging format dynamically: metadata and pinned
  images are read from tutorial packages at runtime, not hard-coded in the
  Dashboard, so tutorial packages can change without a Dashboard release
- Verify the gallery and launch mechanics against tutorial packages that
  conform to the format, covering both launch paths

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given tutorial packages conforming to the packaging format, the Dashboard
  shows a tutorial gallery listing them with their metadata.
- Given a user with a project, when they launch a notebook tutorial from the
  gallery, then a workbench opens in their project with the tutorial notebook
  (measured by successful workbench creation and notebook availability).
- Given a user with a project, when they launch a pipeline tutorial from the
  gallery, then the pipeline is imported into their project (measured by the
  imported pipeline being available to run).
- A tutorial package can be added or updated without a Dashboard release and
  the gallery reflects it (packages are consumed dynamically per the packaging
  format).
- The gallery and launch work with any conformant tutorial package, verified
  against at least one conformant notebook tutorial package and one conformant
  pipeline tutorial package.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook,
  or importing the pipeline).

# RHAISTRAT-9019 Decomposition: Curated getting-started tutorial gallery

Strategy status: Refinement Done, priority Major. The strategy delivers a curated
tutorial gallery made of three architecturally distinct kinds of work (per its
own problem statement): product code (the Dashboard gallery and one-click launch
mechanics), authored content (six curated, tested tutorials), and documentation,
plus a packaging format that decouples tutorial versioning and testability from
Dashboard releases. The decomposition splits along work-product type and
component boundaries accordingly.

## Triage Assessment

Not below-threshold and not docs-only. The strategy spans four components
(Dashboard, Notebooks, Data Science Pipelines, Documentation) and multiple
distinct work streams — code implementation, substantive content authoring, and
documentation — with different owners and review processes, so the
multiple-distinct-work-streams escape condition applies and a full
decomposition is produced.
